messages:
sam: FYI seeing a p99 spike on hosted API US-EAST-1 starting ~11:36 UTC. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~480ms, p99 up to ~1.2s. Queue depth on runtime nodes spiked to 98% of max_queue_depth.

maria: Copy. Any obvious EBS / host issues?

sam: No, infra looks green. I grabbed the runtime traces: lots of requests falling back to kernel 'generic-float' instead of 'attn-optimized' around the spike window. Also KV cache miss rate jumped from 4% -> 28% for many tenants.

jordan: Did we roll any kernel-selection heuristics or model variant updates this morning?

sam: We did a small kernel selector tweak at 11:20 that loosened sequence-length grouping to reduce latency for short chats. Hypothesis: that change increased heterogeneity in batches so the runtime sometimes can't pick the fast kernel and falls back, + more KV cache churn.

lee: Quick metrics dump: `metric:hosted/runtime/queue_depth avg=0.74 p95=0.98` `metric:hosted/runtime/kvcache_miss tenant=acme-inc rate=0.28` `metric:hosted/runtime/kernels/fallback_count=4300` between 11:30-11:45.

sam: Logs: ``
[11:36:12] WARN select_kernel: chosen=generic-float fallback_reason=kernel-mismatch batch_size=16 seq_lengths=[8,256,12,34,...]
[11:36:12] INFO kvcache: miss tenant=acme-inc key_prefix=chat:prefetch id=0x4f2a ttl_expired=false
``

maria: acme-inc is a heavy embedder tenant, might be sending mix of long and short sequences. That can blow up batching heuristics. If their requests interleave, KV cache prefetch may thrash.

jordan: Can we confirm noisy-tenant pattern? show top-tenants by qps and miss-rate.

sam: Top QPS tenants during window: acme-inc=32% total QPS, shoply=9%, internal-tests=5%. acme-inc had 65% of kernel fallback events.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-8423 "hosted p99 spike - kernel fallback + KV miss thrash". Pager notified on-call.

lee: Suggestion: temporary rate-limit burst for acme-inc to smooth interleaving + revert selector tweak to previous grouping threshold. That should reduce heterogeneity in batches and let 'attn-optimized' dominate.

maria: Agreed. Also add a quick kvcache instrumentation: track prefetch queue length and prefetch latencies per tenant. We might be evicting prefixes too aggressively.

jordan: I'll push a temporary per-tenant prefetch cap (limit prefetch concurrent requests to 4) and add a throttle rule to cap acme-inc burst to 20rps. Pushing now.

sam: After cap deployed at 11:46, queue depth dropped to 0.43 and p95 back to ~200ms within 3m. KV miss rate for acme-inc fell to 9% by 11:53. Fallback_count delta reduced by ~82%.

maria: Good remediation signal. Next steps: revert the kernel selector tweak in canary, add unit tests to ensure sequence-length grouping doesn't create pathological batches, and schedule a follow-up to tune kvcache prefetch eviction policy.

lee: Also file a perf-regression alert for kernel-selection changes so future tweaks require a small canary and perf smoke test across mixed-length traffic.

sam: I'll open the issue and link traces. ACTIONS: sam -> create INC postmortem + perf issue (#PR-XXXX), jordan -> keep temporary caps until next deploy, maria -> add kvcache instrumentation, lee -> add alerting rule.

devops-bot: deploy job 5462 completed to hosted-runtime-canary (revert selector changes).

sam: Re-check plan: revert in canary first, run 30m mixed-length replay (we have historical traces), then roll if stable.

maria: Also add a small change to the kernel selector to prefer kernel affinity when batch heterogeneity > threshold. That should avoid fallback spikes. Will propose in PR this afternoon.

jordan: Keeping caps in place for now. Will post numbers in the incident doc. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks all. Marking this thread resolved once postmortem is up. :eyes:
